solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pointer points, showing only the outskirts perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters gathered here may be arranged some other way
only the outskirts of the word showing are kept, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Something that points the way seems to show only the edges of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only the outskirts' of 'showing' gives SG; add POINTS and 'perhaps' rearranges the eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside post with arms bearing directions is a fingerpost that indicates the way, a kind of pointer.

clue.text: Rare box, shame free of meat

parts.note: to spar is to box

indicators.note: free of means the meat word is removed from shame

parts.note: ham is a meat

explanation.surface: An unusual boxing match, disgracefully without any meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinly scattered and scarce, in short supply.

clue.text: So many stars appearing loose, not straight about it

indicators.note: about it means the word for not straight goes around the word for loose

parts.note: gay is slang for not heterosexual
lax means slack or loose

explanation.surface: Lots of celebrities look relaxed and unconventional.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge system of stars such as the Milky Way, so a vast number of them.

clue.text: Model's leg in traction?

parts.note: pins is slang for legs
a leg in traction is held up in the air

explanation.surface: A fashion model with an injured leg in hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A glamour picture or the person in it, pinned up on a wall.

clue.text: Untruth in Father Christmas not entirely obvious

indicators.note: in means the untruth goes inside the trimmed Christmas figure
not entirely means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Santa is Father Christmas
a lie is an untruth

explanation.surface: The lie that Father Christmas exists is not completely obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' drops the final letter of the Christmas figure's name, and 'in' then places the untruth inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Most noticeable or prominent, standing out.

clue.text: Shift rod

definitions.meaning: to change over or move from one thing to another
a thin flexible stick or cane

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to change position; as a noun a slender whippy stick used for beating.

clue.text: Crustacean felt aware when swimming

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: A creature in the water sensing it is being watched.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny freshwater crustacean such as Daphnia, which moves in jerky hops.

clue.text: Cattle taking half hour off to get drier

indicators.note: off means the letters are rearranged, as when something goes off
half keeps the first two letters of the word hour

explanation.surface: Cows given half an hour's break to dry out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' of 'hour' is HO; with CATTLE, 'off' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth used to dry washed crockery, so a thing that dries.

clue.text: Turn criminal into Nazi killer

indicators.note: into means the shuffled letters go inside the Nazi's name

parts.note: Rudolf Hess was a leading Nazi

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are bent out of shape

explanation.surface: Someone goes bad and becomes a Nazi murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges TURN to UNTR, which goes 'into' HESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who hunts game kills it, like the goddess Diana.

clue.text: Everything considered, t helt helot ot?

parts.note: the letters read THEL THELOT OT, that is the words the lot placed inside another copy of the lot

explanation.surface: A deliberately jumbled string of letters ending in a puzzled question mark.
explanation.walkthrough: Close up the spaces: THEL + THELOT + OT is 'the lot' sitting inside 'the lot'. 'The lot' means ALL, so the picture reads ALL IN ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means taking everything into account, on the whole.

clue.text: Music that's painful?

definitions.meaning: a melody or passage of a tune
an injury such as a pulled muscle that hurts

explanation.surface: Music that hurts the ears.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a passage of melody and a muscle injury from overstretching.

clue.text: Hit head in short circuit

indicators.note: head in picks the first letter of short

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a track

explanation.surface: A blow to the head that causes a short circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack with an open hand, a blow.

clue.text: It's the other petition

parts.note: the other is a coy British euphemism for sex
a petition is an appeal or request

explanation.surface: A coy description of a petition about something unmentionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' in the old sense of personal magnetism, as in the 'It girl'; 'the other' is British slang for sex, as in 'a bit of the other'.
explanation.definitionFit: 'It' as a noun once meant sexual attractiveness, the quality made famous by Clara Bow.

clue.text: Master in schoolboy's possession

definitions.meaning: one who governs or is in charge
an item kept in a pencil case for drawing lines

explanation.surface: A head teacher found in a pupil's satchel.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a sovereign who governs and the straight measuring strip carried by every pupil.

clue.text: Don't eat like a sprinter

explanation.surface: Advice to skip meals, as an athlete might.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means abstain from food; as an adjective it means quick-moving.

clue.text: Distribute ration and pop out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: Hand out the rations, then nip out.
explanation.definitionFit: To share out or allot portions to people.

clue.text: Many should keep at a system of exercise

indicators.note: should keep means the word for many holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: piles, as in piles of money, means lots or many
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lots of people ought to stick to a fitness regime.
explanation.definitionFit: A named body-conditioning method focusing on core strength, developed by Joseph Pilates.

clue.text: Comprehensive school's head, sorrowful

indicators.note: head picks the first letter of school's

parts.note: weeping means crying, sorrowful

explanation.surface: A comprehensive school's headteacher is in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comprehensive' looks like a British state school; it is the adjective meaning wide-ranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Wide-ranging and all-embracing, as in sweeping changes.

clue.text: Sob and whine uncontrollably, as bit of a chicken

indicators.note: uncontrollably suggests letters thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Crying and moaning, like a cowardly person.
explanation.definitionFit: The forked breastbone of a bird, pulled apart for luck.

clue.text: Attack favourite dog

parts.note: to whip is to beat or lash, an attack
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Someone's beloved hound turns aggressive.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender racing breed resembling a small greyhound.

clue.text: US president thanks us?

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks
us from the newspaper's viewpoint is the FT

explanation.surface: An American leader expressing gratitude to the people.
explanation.definitionFit: William Howard Taft was the 27th president of the United States.

clue.text: Something to chew on about a Pacific island

indicators.note: about means the chewy word goes around the next letter

parts.note: gum is chewed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Chewing something while on a Pacific island.
explanation.definitionFit: A US territory in the Mariana Islands of the western Pacific.

clue.text: Coming in strongest, a potent war force

indicators.note: coming in signals letters found inside the following words

explanation.surface: Arriving at full strength, a powerful army.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nazi secret police, a feared force of the Second World War era.

clue.text: A second president turning up as very simple life-form

parts.note: mo is a moment or second

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue turns the name upwards, backwards

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln

explanation.surface: Another president reverses into a primitive organism.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-celled organism that moves by changing shape.

clue.text: Cricket side beginning to hope, veteran waiting to come in

parts.note: on is the leg side in cricket

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of hope

parts.note: old means veteran

explanation.surface: A cricket team hoping for a veteran player's arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on (or leg) side is the half of the field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone caller kept waiting before being connected, paused.

clue.text: Taken by police, the registration number

indicators.note: taken by signals letters carried within the following words

explanation.surface: Police noting down a car's registration number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is read as 'something that numbs', an old anaesthetic; the surface wants a numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: An anaesthetic gas that deadens feeling, so something that makes one numb.

clue.text: Networker providing reversing tank

indicators.note: reversing turns the word for providing backwards

parts.note: if means providing, on condition that
the Sherman was a US Second World War tank

explanation.surface: Someone who makes connections supplies a tank that goes backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler using nets, playfully called a networker.

clue.text: Wise guy in tree

definitions.meaning: a senior respected person in a community
a small tree bearing dark berries

explanation.surface: A sage sits in a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a senior figure valued for wisdom and the shrub Sambucus.

clue.text: As a symbol, one like a cornet

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
an ice-cream cornet is cone-shaped, conic

explanation.surface: A trumpet-like instrument stands as an emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing something serving as an emblem or representative image.

clue.text: Beach that is to disappear in US city

parts.note: a beach is sand
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
to go is to vanish

explanation.surface: A beach that vanishes in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: A major Californian city on the Pacific coast near Mexico.

clue.text: Author a shade elusive in the end

parts.note: green is a colour or shade

indicators.note: in the end picks the closing letter of elusive

explanation.surface: A writer whose tint is ultimately hard to pin down.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene was an English novelist, author of Brighton Rock.

clue.text: Extremes of greed consuming chap from the FT? Epicure

indicators.note: consuming means those two letters wrap around the next piece
extremes of means only the first and last letters of greed are used

parts.note: the newspaper's own man is our man, said from the FT's point of view

explanation.surface: A greedy Financial Times journalist turns out to be a lover of fine food.
explanation.definitionFit: A connoisseur of good food and eating, a gastronome.
